claim: Acquire the public repository epachayan/indus-script at commit 5c14a01f44296a01256a34e7e5e5e9fd82d9a67f and record what its seal tables contain. Its README describes a 709-row transcription of Mackay's 1938 "Tabulation of Seals" (type, size in inches, material, block/house/room or street, level relative to the DK datum, field number) and a 560-row transcription of Marshall's 1931 table (type, size, material, excavation area, depth below the surface), both checked against an OCR cross-check. A Zenodo record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23281781, CC BY 4.0) describes the same work; its version note says the tables were produced by an AI model, and it holds only a preprint PDF, so the repository is the data source.
title: Acquire the machine-readable Mackay 1938 and Marshall 1931 seal tables at a pinned commit

claim: Which Mackay 1938 and Marshall 1931 seal-table rows correspond to which CISI M-numbers and local Lipi objects, and what size, material, findspot and level does each joined object gain?
title: Join the Mackay and Marshall seal tables to CISI M-numbers and the local Mohenjo-daro objects
